entities.summary: Cornelius Vanderbilt IV was a newspaper publisher, journalist, author, and military officer. He was an outcast of high society, and was disinherited by his parents when he became a newspaper publisher. He desired to live a "normal" life but was burdened by large debt and could not maintain the lifestyle associated with his family's social position to which he had become accustomed. Cornelius Vanderbilt IV was a performers & entertainers from Staten Island (1898-04-30, Staten Island–1974-07-07). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to economic history and geopolitics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a newspaper publisher and journalist, Cornelius Vanderbilt IV played a significant role in shaping public opinion during the late 19th century. His publications contributed to the growth of urban newspapers, influencing local politics and social issues.
